clue.text: Corrupt "haves" all at once inherit our greatest public asset

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or debased, so the letters of the following words are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that greedy people suddenly inherit what belongs to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The 21 letters of HAVES ALL AT ONCE INHERIT rearrange into the three words. The puzzle marks the 70th anniversary of Britain's state-funded health system, founded in 1948.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's state-funded medical system is often described by the public as the country's most cherished institution.

clue.text: Regularly sneers at poor old counsellor

indicators.note: regularly means taking every second letter of the words sneers at poor, at even intervals

explanation.surface: Someone habitually mocks a needy elderly adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of 'sneers at poor'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, the aged king of Pylos was the wise adviser to the Greeks, so his name stands for any elderly mentor.

clue.text: Hospital study following Bert's last suture

indicators.note: following means the hospital and study pieces come after the letter from Bert
Bert's last points to the final letter of the name Bert

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A medical note: the stitching came from a hospital study after Bert's last operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the T from Bert ahead of H and READ.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical stitch is made with a strand of fibre, and the strand itself can be called a suture.

clue.text: Rusting, lidless box hid a can containing nothing

indicators.note: lidless means each of the words box and hid loses its top, that is its first letter

parts.note: the two words box and hid are written out as they stand

indicators.note: containing means the can piece holds the nothing piece inside it

parts.note: a tin is a can
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A rusty box without its lid concealed an empty can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lidless' beheads both 'box' and 'hid', giving OX and ID; 'containing' puts O inside TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust forms when iron combines chemically with oxygen, so rusting is a case of that chemical process.

clue.text: Ensure bandage moved lower

definitions.note: here a lower is something that lows, that is a mooing animal

indicators.note: moved means the letters of ensure bandage are shifted about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A first-aid instruction: make sure the dressing is shifted further down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' reads as 'further down' but is one that lows, i.e. moos: a breed of Scottish beef cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle low, so a crossword can call a cow or bullock a lower; this is a breed of Scottish beef cattle.

clue.text: See 1
Superior neighbour sounded weird

indicators.note: sounded means the lake name is spoken, and the spoken form is spelt as a different word

parts.note: Lake Erie lies next to Lake Superior among North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A haughty person living next door made a strange noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' looks like 'snooty' but is Lake Superior, whose neighbouring Great Lake is Erie.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weird is strange and unsettling, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Are still taking pulse, for example of Flora

indicators.note: taking means the first piece takes in the second, holding it inside

parts.note: to lie is to remain still and at rest
metre is the regular beat or pulse of verse or music

explanation.surface: A doctor checking that someone is still breathing, before an aside about a Flora.
explanation.walkthrough: Flora with a capital is the plant life of a region; a linden is one tree in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora means plants collectively, and the linden is one specimen of that plant life.

clue.text: Barbarians entertaining very French lady after game

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so the barbarians piece goes around the French word

parts.note: the Huns were barbarian invaders of the Roman Empire
tres is French for very

explanation.surface: Rough tribesmen playing host to a very French woman once the match is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is not a sports match but animals hunted, so the 'lady after game' is a woman who hunts.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who pursues animals for sport is chasing game, as Diana does in myth.

clue.text: See 1
People in court to condemn Jeremy Hunt neglecting the sick

indicators.note: sick means unwell or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Jeremy Hunt was the UK Health Secretary when this puzzle appeared
the word the supplies letters that are taken out of the mix

explanation.surface: A jab at a Health Secretary, Jeremy Hunt, who people want to see judged for ignoring the ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neglecting the' means THE is left out of JEREMY HUNT, and 'sick' jumbles what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a jury sit in court and decide whether to convict, so they are there to pass judgement.

clue.text: Right now I fib about blood group, for good reason

parts.note: just as in just now means at this very moment

indicators.note: about means the fib piece goes around the blood group letter

parts.note: a fib is a small lie, a piece of fiction
A is one of the blood groups

explanation.surface: A patient admits to lying about their blood group, insisting it was for a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the blood group A inside FICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A justification is a sound defence or reason given for an action, so good reason is a plain synonym.

clue.text: First to admire Mr Aneurin Bevan, our revolutionary 5 reformer?

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the run of initial letters is read backwards
first to points to the opening letter of each of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: Praise for Aneurin Bevan, founder of the British health service, as its great radical.
explanation.walkthrough: Initials of 'admire Mr Aneurin Bevan our' give AMABO; 'revolutionary' turns it round. 5 is HEALTH: the US president behind the Affordable Care Act.
explanation.definitionFit: The 44th US president pushed through the Affordable Care Act, a major overhaul of American medical insurance.

clue.text: Be rude about 'Arry, chap with scalpel

parts.note: to diss someone is to be rude about them, slang from disrespect
harry means to harass, as does hector; the apostrophe shows the H dropped, so the verb loses its H too

explanation.surface: Someone insults 'Arry, a man holding a surgical knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arry is Harry with the H dropped, Cockney style. Read harry as the verb 'harass', whose synonym hector also drops its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cuts up bodies or specimens to study them works with a scalpel, an anatomist's tool.

clue.text: Rebellious 1 5 9 donning uniforms with singular irritability

indicators.note: donning means putting on clothes, so the uniforms piece goes around the health service letters

parts.note: liveries are the uniforms worn by servants or company staff

indicators.note: rebellious suggests revolting, turning over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the three linked lights make up the British health service, abbreviated NHS
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Health service staff in revolt put on uniforms and get very bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 5 9' points to the three linked lights, abbreviated as Britain's health service initials; 'Rebellious' turns them round and 'donning' wraps the uniforms around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A liverish person is grumpy, the old idea being that a disordered liver made you bad-tempered.

clue.text: Sat at home twirling surgical instrument

indicators.note: twirling means spinning round, so the letters of sat at home are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sat at home spinning a medical tool in their fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twirling' rearranges SATATHOME.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a clamp or similar device a surgeon uses to stop bleeding, so it is a kind of surgical tool.

clue.text: 10 new non-invasive procedures advanced the study of feet

indicators.note: advanced means brought forward, so the procedures piece moves to the front

parts.note: scans, such as ultrasound, look inside the body without cutting
the figure 10 is read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Ten fresh medical scans have moved forward research into foot problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advanced' puts SCANS before ION. 'feet' are metrical feet in verse, not body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Analysing the rhythm of verse means dividing lines into metrical feet, and this is the term for that analysis.

clue.text: American stops small community rejecting very bad treatment

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing out, so the very letter is removed
stops means plugs a gap, so the American piece is put inside the community piece

parts.note: a village is a small community

explanation.surface: An American blocks a village from refusing appalling treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' plugs the American into the community; 'rejecting' then throws out the very letter. 'small community' is one piece, not 'small' as an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-treatment or abuse is bad treatment, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Allocated by month: care reduced, deadlines trashed

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the letters are thrown into disorder
reduced means cut short, so the word care loses its final letter

parts.note: the word care is written out as it stands

explanation.surface: Health service services cut back and every deadline ruined, under a monthly plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts CARE to CAR; 'trashed' scrambles CAR plus DEADLINES.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something into a dated schedule month by month is to enter it in a diary of the year.

clue.text: Attempt to raise spirits of Irishman with case of champagne

parts.note: Sean is a common Irish man's name

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Cheering someone up by giving an Irishman a crate of fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise spirits' reads as cheer up, but means summoning ghosts. 'case of' takes the outer letters of 'champagne', CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting in which people try to contact the dead is an effort to call up ghosts.

clue.text: One behind the other in Accident & Emergency

parts.note: the answer sits inside the words Accident & Emergency once the ampersand is read out as the word and: the last letter of Accident, the and, and the start of Emergency

explanation.surface: Someone queuing in a hospital casualty department.
explanation.walkthrough: Read '&' as AND: accidenT AND EMergency.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things in line, the second behind the first, are arranged like riders on a two-seat bicycle.

clue.text: Pain of north European country losing monarch

parts.note: EUR is an abbreviation for European

indicators.note: losing means dropping, so the monarch letters come out of the country

parts.note: Algeria is a country in North Africa
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of the British queen

explanation.surface: The ache of a northern European nation that has lost its king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European country' looks like one piece, but European gives EUR and the country is Algeria, in Africa; 'losing' drops its ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve pain, often sharp and stabbing, is the medical sense; it is a kind of ache.

clue.text: Local London football team spurned by Poles

indicators.note: spurned by means rejected, so the pole letters are thrown out of the team name

parts.note: Arsenal is a north London football club
S and N are the south and north poles

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood London football club snubbed by Polish fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like Polish people but means the magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something limited to a particular area or region, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Theatre cancelling 50% of surgical procedures

indicators.note: cancelling half the letters leaves the first five of the ten

parts.note: operations are surgical procedures

explanation.surface: An operating theatre calling off half of its scheduled operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' looks like the operating theatre but is the art form; half of OPERATIONS is OPERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is a form of musical drama, and an opera house is a kind of theatre.

clue.text: Current wife describing time in MRI machines?

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the wife piece is put around the time piece

parts.note: Mrs is the title of a married woman
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: An electric current and a wife describing the time she spent in a scanner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense, to draw a line round something, so the wife piece encircles the time piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A scanner that produces pictures of the inside of the body is a device that makes images; the question mark flags the coinage.

clue.text: "Skint!", one dental nurse said monotonously

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close, so the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A dental nurse grumbles flatly that she has no money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurse' looks like the dental nurse, but is a verb: the words skINT ONE Dental hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To chant or recite on a single unvarying pitch is to speak in a flat drone.

clue.text: Require extremely large hypodermic?

parts.note: to require something is to need it

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of large

explanation.surface: Asking whether a really big injection is called for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' reads as 'very' but takes the ends of 'large', LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypodermic syringe delivers its dose through a fine hollow spike, so the word can name the spike.

clue.text: Available drug seized by frantic matrons

indicators.note: seized by means held tight, so the drug letter goes inside the jumbled matrons
frantic means wildly agitated, so the letters of matrons are shaken up

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug is available, grabbed by panicking senior nurses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantic' rearranges MATRONS; 'seized by' puts E inside. A matron is the senior nurse in charge of a British hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up and running and ready for use is in operation, a plain sense of the two-word phrase.
